# Troubleshooting

## Postgres Connection Timeouts

If `sqlpipe` times out during a Postgres connection, read the network logs.

If a firewall blocks port `5432`, update the firewall rules to allow traffic.

If you connect across a virtual private network, make sure that the network connection is active.

If the target database host is slow, open the `sqlpipe` config file.

To extend the wait time, increase the `PG_TIMEOUT` value in the config file.

If the target database exceeds maximum connections, restart inactive database sessions.

If the problem continues, test the connection with `pg_isready`.

## S3 Permission Errors

If `sqlpipe` shows an S3 permission error, read the AWS identity config.

If the S3 bucket policy denies access, grant the `s3:PutObject` permission to your IAM role.

If you read data from S3, grant the `s3:GetObject` permission to your IAM role.

If your IAM policy uses explicit denial rules, remove the denial rules for the target bucket.

If you use temporary AWS credentials, make sure that the session token is active.

If the bucket uses AWS KMS encryption, grant the `kms:GenerateDataKey` permission to your role.

To test your access permissions, run the `aws s3 ls` command against the target bucket.
